title: `AVG` of integers: a `DOUBLE` within a bound of the exact mean
verdict: `DOUBLE`; for exact sum s and count n: |s| <= 2^53, one of the two doubles around s/n (s/n itself when it is a double); |s| > 2^53, within a relative bound of s/n that covers every path (constant open)
description: For the non-NULL values with exact sum `s` and count `n`, `avg` of `INTEGER` or `BIGINT` returns a double `r` with: `|s| <= 2^53`, `r` is one of the two doubles around `s / n`, and `s / n` itself when that is a double; `|s| > 2^53`, `r` is within a relative bound of `s / n` that covers every path below (the sum rounded to a double, then divided; the 80-bit quotient rounded again; the two-rounding cast of a negative sum). Fable's estimate of the constant is 4 * 2^-53; the owner of the profile change (12d-2) derives and proves it. Which member of the set comes back depends on the platform's `long double`, on the plan's shape, on sibling aggregates, on statistics and on optimizer settings, so the set is the fact and no shape is. The paragraphs below are the evidence.

`avg` has one overload per integer width it names, `SMALLINT`, `INTEGER`, `BIGINT` and `HUGEINT`, and each returns `DOUBLE`; there is no integer result. `TINYINT` has none: the binder takes the overload with the cheapest implicit cast, and a cast to `BIGINT` costs 101 against 110 for `SMALLINT`, so `avg(TINYINT)` runs the `BIGINT` one.

`SMALLINT`: the sum is an `int64_t` (`RegularAdd`, unchecked, out of reach below 2^48 rows) and the result `double(sum) / double(count)`. `INTEGER` and `BIGINT`: the sum is an exact `HUGEINT` (`AddToHugeint`) and the native finalize is `long double(sum) / long double(count)`, rounded to `DOUBLE`. `long double` is 80-bit on x86-64 Linux and the same as `double` on arm64 macOS and MSVC, so the last bit of a mean can depend on the platform.
No values gives NULL. The width dispatch is one template instantiation per width (`GetAverageAggregate`), which is what lets this reading cover `i8` to `i64`.

Round 4 (probes): `avg` of TINYINT and SMALLINT is a DOUBLE (126.5, 32766.5). `avg` of 2^63 - 1, 2^63 - 2, 2^63 - 3 is 9.223372036854776e+18 and of 2^53 + 1, 2^53 + 2 is 9007199254740994.0 on any platform. The last bit depends on `long double`: `avg` of 2^53 + 1, 0, 0 is 3002399751580330.5 on macOS arm64, where the sum is rounded to a double before the division; an 80-bit `long double` would give the exact mean 3002399751580331, and the x86-64 Linux wheel gave 3002399751580330.5 as macOS arm64 does (round 5).

The docs are silent on `avg`'s DOUBLE result, the `long double` division and the overload `TINYINT` takes: a docs gap. No upstream test pins the platform-dependent last bit; it may change between versions.

Which path runs depends on the plan. DuckDB 2.0.0's optimizer rewrites `AVG(x)` to `CAST(SUM(x) AS DOUBLE) / CAST(COUNT(x) AS DOUBLE)` (`AvgRewriteRule`, `aggregate_function_rewriter.cpp:70-172`) when the aggregate has no groups, and with groups when a `SUM` or `COUNT` of the same child stands beside it. A grouped mean on its own and a window mean keep the native finalize. Rounds 5 and 6 (probes `avg_int.py`, `avg_int_shapes.py`) ran both on x86-64 Linux: the rewritten shapes give one division in doubles of the sum rounded to a double (the model's value) on every input tried, and the native shapes give the 80-bit quotient rounded again to a double. Where the two differ, in 300 of 300 grouped pairs of each kind (a sum below 2^53 over 1,025 to 19,999 rows; a sum from 2^53 to 2^62 over 2 to 1,999 rows), the native shapes return the 80-bit value, one unit in the last place above or below the model's value in about equal numbers. On arm64 macOS every shape gives the model's value, as `long double` is a double there. Random groups of 2 to 4,999 values below 2^40 gave the model's value in all 3,000 groups in every shape: the two readings differ for about one group in 2,000 to 4,000, so a sample that size may not show it.

`HUGEINT` to `DOUBLE` of a negative value rounds twice (`CastBigintToFloating`, `hugeint.cpp:458-469`: `-REAL_T(UINT64_MAX - lower) - 1`), so the sum of a negative total of magnitude 2^53 and above can come out one unit in the last place from the correctly rounded value on every path that casts the sum: the rewritten means and the native ones. Round 6 gave, for 300 negative sums of magnitude 2^53 to 2^63 over 1 to 49 values, 1 group off the model on arm64 macOS in each shape except the ungrouped one, and 65 on x86-64 Linux in the native shapes (`GROUP BY` and windows; 37 above and 28 below the model's value), 1 in `GROUP BY` beside a `SUM` and 0 ungrouped.
reference: `avg_int_result` follows the plan's declared output type (#209). With `fp64` the reference averages the integers' conversions to doubles (`parseMeasure`), so it rounds each value and then the sum, where DuckDB rounds the exact sum once; both are within #85's bound.

With `i64` the reference is the exact mean truncated toward zero (`AggFn.iavg`); sverify's DuckDB SQL writes it as `CAST(SUM(v) // COUNT(v) AS BIGINT)` (`sverify_duckdb/dialect.py`, `int_avg`), on the exact `HUGEINT` sum, so DuckDB's `AVG` is not used there.
